[g2 9c0204adaa] **Stale-adapter resume skip: manifest-at-START + presence-based "done" ships a prior fingerprint's adapter as the retrained cell.** `scripts/issue2225_train.py:535` writes the fingerprint manifest at cell START (before training); `should_skip` (397–414) skips iff fingerprint match AND (`_local_done` — adapter files merely EXIST locally, 408 — OR `_hf_complete` — files merely exist under the HF prefix, 411). Neither leg binds the artifact to the fingerprint that PRODUCED it, and a non-skip re-run never wipes the prior run's files. Trace: cell completes under fingerprint F1 → code-fix/direction-rebuild flips to F2 → re-run writes the F2 manifest at START → crashes mid-train (`save_strategy="no"` writes nothing until the final save, so the F1 files survive untouched) → relaunch sees F2==F2 AND F1-era `adapter_model.safetensors` present → SKIP. The stale adapter is then evaluated as the retrained cell — a silent confound of the primary result. The whole-HEAD `code_sha` field makes the trigger LIKELY: any commit invalidates ALL 81 cells, so one mid-wave OOM/preempt during a crash-fix round strands several cells exactly in this state. Minimal fixes (either closes it): (a) on a non-skip run, unlink `out_dir/adapter_config.json` + `adapter_model.safetensors` immediately after writing the START manifest AND record an artifact-binding field (e.g. adapter file sha or `completed_at`) written only at save time that `_local_done`/`_hf_complete` require; or (b) move to END-manifest done-marker semantics ({fingerprint, completed, uploaded}). Fix must cover the HF leg too — the F1-era upload also satisfies `_hf_complete` under an F2 manifest.

[g4 8b2c549c65] **Every pod sentinel is written into a SUBDIRECTORY the VM poller's drain glob cannot see.** `scripts/issue2225_dispatch.sh:70`: `LOG_ROOT="${EPM_I2225_LOG_ROOT:-/workspace/logs/issue-2225}"` is passed as `logs_dir` to `issue778_lib.write_results_sentinel`, so sentinels land at `/workspace/logs/issue-2225/issue-2225-epm_results-<epoch>.json`. `scripts/poll_pipeline.py:2321-2333` drains `/workspace/logs/issue-2225-*.json` (path-terminal, non-recursive); the results-presence probe (`poll_pipeline.py:2044`) is equally top-level; plan §9 `phase_outputs` pins the top-level contract explicitly. ## DIRECTION of the change — read this before comparing any numbers

Stating the direction explicitly, because "the parser got better" does not say which way
the numbers move:

1. **Per-DRAW parsed values: BIT-IDENTICAL.** Step 5 fires ONLY on inputs that previously
   returned `None`. Any draw that parsed at steps 1-4 returns exactly what it returned
   before. Nothing that was already a number changes.
2. **Parse-fail / content-drop RATES: DOWN.** Previously-dropped labelled-score draws are
   now scored, so `n_content_dropped` falls and `n_scored` rises. This is the headline
   effect.
3. **Per-ITEM and aggregate MEANS: CAN MOVE, in either direction.** This is the nuance to
   NOT gloss: an item whose mean was computed over its surviving draws now averages a
   recovered draw as well, so the item mean shifts by whatever that draw's value is
   relative to the old mean. Sign is not predictable a priori. So (1) is a statement about
   individual draws, NOT about aggregates — do not read it as "scores are unchanged".
4. Because the recovered draws are OUTCOME-CORRELATED (the judge breaks format precisely
   on ambiguous / borderline items), the shift in (3) is NOT mean-zero noise: it
   preferentially restores borderline cases. That is the whole point of fixing rather than
   waiving, and it also means the shift is a genuine measurement improvement, not drift.

## Consequence for cross-boundary comparisons

Any DROP-RATE or n_scored comparison that straddles this commit is a mixed-instrument
comparison and MUST name the parser-version split — the same convention #2109's advisory
established for step 4. Banked caches store PARSED results and are never re-parsed, so a
cached item keeps its pre-step-5 mean while a freshly-judged item gets the post-step-5
mean; a run that mixes cached and fresh items across the boundary mixes instruments at the
ITEM level. If a sibling needs post-step-5 semantics for already-banked items, it must
re-judge them against a FRESH cache — a cache-served re-run reports a 0% drop rate and
silently keeps the old means (the llm-judging rule 24(ii) cache-masking hazard; #2225 hit
exactly this and archived its gate cache rather than reuse it).
